We use it to study facets of amplituhedron cells, and to show that some of them do not lie in zero loci of dual canonical basis elements, disproving a conjecture by T. Lam \cite{LamGP}.

hep-th.title: Periodic charge oscillations in the Proca theory
hep-th.author: Bogdan Damski
hep-th.abstract: We consider the Proca theory of the real massive vector field. There is a locally conserved 4-current operator in such a theory, which one may use to define the charge operator. Accordingly, there are charged states in which the expectation value of the charge operator is non-zero. We take a close look at the charge operator and study the dynamics of the certain class of charged states. For this purpose, we discuss the mean electric field and 4-current in such states. The mean electric field has the periodically oscillating Coulomb component, whose presence explains the periodic charge oscillations. A complementary insight at such a phenomenon is provided by the mean 4-current, whose discussion leads to the identification of a certain paradox. Last but not least, we show that there is a shock wave propagating in the studied system, which affects analyticity of the mean electric field and 4-current.

hep-th.title: Non-equilibrium dynamics of dipole-charged fields in the Proca theory
hep-th.author: Bogdan Damski
hep-th.abstract: We discuss the dynamics of field configurations encoded in the certain class of electric (magnetic) dipole-charged states in the Proca theory of the real massive vector field. We construct such states so as to ensure that the long distance structure of the mean electromagnetic field in them is initially set by the formula describing the electromagnetic field of the electric (magnetic) dipole. We analyze then how such a mean electromagnetic field evolves in time. We find that far away from the center of the initial field configuration, the long range component of the mean electromagnetic field harmonically oscillates, which leads to the phenomenon of the periodic oscillations of the electric (magnetic) dipole moment. We also find that near the center of the initial field configuration, the mean electromagnetic field escapes from its initial arrangement and a spherical shock wave propagating with the speed of light appears in the studied system. A curious configuration of the axisymmetric mean electric field is found to accompany the mean magnetic field in magnetic dipole-charged states.

hep-th.title: Examining the Anomalous Nature of Chiral Effects in Thermodynamics
hep-th.author: Rémy Larue, Jérémie Quevillon, Diego Saviot
hep-th.abstract: Quantum anomalies give rise to novel transport phenomena, including the generation of a current in a relativistic fluid due to the presence of magnetic field or vorticity. We present an exclusive and direct computation of the chiral anomaly in the adiabatic regime within the path integral for a massless fermion on a generic electromagnetic and curved background, including local temperature and chemical potential. We identify new quantum-thermodynamical contributions to the breaking of axial symmetry which induce the Chiral Separation and Vortical Effects.

hep-th.title: Four-dimensional supersymmetric massive QED
hep-th.author: A. C. Lehum, J. R. Nascimento, A. Yu. Petrov
hep-th.abstract: We study a four-dimensional $\mathcal N=1$ supersymmetric Proca model with an explicit mass term for a real vector superfield and a generalized transverse kinetic operator. Although it displays no gauge redundancy in Proca variables, for local kinetic operators the model is the exact classical unitary-gauge form of the minimal Abelian $\mathcal N=1$ Stueckelberg realization, with the SQED-like exponential as its minimal gauge-covariant matter coupling. We compute the Kählerian contribution to the one-loop effective action using both the background-field Hessian and an independent supergraph organization. In the minimal model the background-dependent divergence is local and is absorbed by the matter Kähler normalization, and the finite local terms left by the subtraction remain scheme dependent. At $\alpha=0$, an anomaly-free minimal Stueckelberg formulation supports a conditional perturbative-renormalizability interpretation for the corresponding minimal theory. For $f(\Box)=\Box+\alpha\Box^2$ we distinguish the exact polynomial model, defined over the full momentum range, from a truncated derivative expansion; in the latter reading, the additional pole and the local matching term are ultraviolet information determined by the completion rather than predictions of the truncated theory.

hep-th.title: Does hot QCD have a conformal manifold in the chiral limit?
hep-th.author: Shi Chen, Aleksey Cherman, Robert D. Pisarski
hep-th.abstract: Recent lattice evidence may suggest the chiral phase transition in QCD is second order for $N_f \ge 2$ massless flavors. We constrain conformal field theory (CFT) descriptions of a critical line in temperature $T$ and imaginary baryon chemical potential $\theta_B = i\mu_B/T$. An 't Hooft anomaly at general $\theta_B$ constrains the transition even at $\theta_B = 0$, leaving only three minimal scenarios. The best-motivated scenario for $N_f\ge3$, and perhaps also $N_f = 2$, is beyond Ginzburg-Landau, featuring a conformal manifold of $\theta_B$-dependent universality classes with an exactly marginal operator related to baryon density.

hep-th.title: Worldline Images for Yang-Mills Theory within Boundaries
hep-th.author: Santiago Christiansen Murguizur, Lucas Manzo, Pablo Pisani
hep-th.abstract: In this article we develop a worldline technique based on the method of images to study the effective action associated to Yang-Mills theories on manifolds with boundaries. We consider the possibility of having either relative or absolute boundary conditions, which are particular types of mixed boundary conditions. Both vector fields and ghost fields are taken into account in this analysis. As a check of our construction, we compute the first three Seeley-DeWitt coefficients of the heat kernel asymptotics. Finally, we employ our technique to calculate the rate of gluon production due to a chromoelectric field background in the presence of a boundary.

hep-th.title: Exact WKB analysis of inverted triple-well: resonance, PT-symmetry breaking, and resurgence
hep-th.author: Syo Kamata, Tatsuhiro Misumi, Cihan Pazarbaşı, Hidetoshi Taya
hep-th.abstract: We study non-Hermitian quantum mechanics of an inverted triple-well potential within the exact WKB framework. For a single classical potential, different Siegert boundary conditions define three distinct quantum problems: the PT-symmetric, resonance, and anti-resonance systems. For each case, we derive the exact quantization condition and construct the associated trans-series solution. By identifying the resurgent structures and cancellations in these non-Hermitian setups, we obtain the median-summed series, clarifying when the spectra are real or complex in accordance with the physical properties of each system. Establishing explicit links to the semi-classical path integral formalism, we elucidate the roles of bounce and bion configurations in these non-Hermitian systems. This analysis predicts PT-symmetry breaking, which we also verify numerically. Using the median quantization conditions, we prove the existence of this symmetry breaking and establish an exact equation for the exceptional point, which emerges as a remarkably simple algebraic relation between the bounce and bion actions. We further show that the median-summed non-perturbative correction to the spectrum vanishes at the exceptional point, while the resurgent structure survives through a universal minimal trans-series. For the resonance and anti-resonance systems, we find that the exact median-summed spectra are related by complex conjugation, representing time reversal in this setting, are necessarily complex, and do not exhibit an exceptional point. Although their spectra differ significantly from the PT-symmetric case, they share the same minimal trans-series. By maintaining explicit links with the path integral saddles and the formal theory of resurgence, our analysis provides a unified and general perspective on the quantization of non-Hermitian theories.

hep-th.title: On the Ising/tricritical-Ising interface: From ${W}_3$ symmetry to Rydberg atoms
hep-th.author: António Antunes, Junchen Rong
hep-th.abstract: We consider interfaces between critical spin-chains in different universality classes, described in the continuum limit by defect/interface conformal field theory (DCFT/ICFT). We focus on a conformal interface between the Tricritical Ising (TIM) and the Ising CFT exploring the possibility of its experimental realizations in the context of Rydberg atom arrays. Our analysis emphasizes non-invertible symmetries and consistency under modular transformations, and uses defect couplings and the defect spectrum -- including in the case of mixed boundary conditions -- to make sharp experimental predictions. The structure of the observables hinges on a newly discovered pattern of emergent ${W}_3$ chiral symmetry for the Tricritical-Ising/Ising interface.

hep-th.title: Brane flows
hep-th.author: Georgios Papadopoulos, Kostas Skenderis
hep-th.abstract: Based on effective D-brane actions, we present a generalisation of the Ricci flow that includes the flow of a theory with a $n$-form field strength for $n\geq 0$. This is a generalisation of both the Ricci flows and the generalised Ricci flows. Following Perelman, we show that flows that keep a suitable field-dependent volume fixed are monotonic. We also show that all steady brane flow solitons are gradient solitons and use this to demonstrate that on some occasions this implies the existence of a Killing vector field that leaves all the other fields invariant. Particular cases of gradient solitons are NS5 and D5 branes, and the volume which is kept fixed in these cases is the T-duality invariant volume (NS5 brane) or its S-dual (D5 brane). We also generalise the above analysis to gravitational actions coupled to form gauge potentials that also exhibit a Chern-Simons type term. We find an alteration is required in the adaptation of Perelman's modification to this case, which yields a new functional that also exhibits a Chern-Simons term. Under suitable assumptions, we proceed to prove the monotonicity of the flow and that all steady flow solitons are gradient solitons. We also explore the consequences of the last statement on the geometry of solitons.

hep-th.title: Chiral Transport in Metric-Affine Geometries
hep-th.author: Miguel A. Vazquez-Mozo
hep-th.abstract: Anomalous transport in equilibrium fermionic fluids chirally coupled to background Weyl-type nonmetricity is studied. A formal descent analysis is carried out in which the dependence of the anomaly polynomial on the nonmetricity tensor is encoded in a Weyl invariant four-form. The constitutive relation of the axial-vector current is evaluated from the equilibrium partition function obtained using transgression techniques, showing the existence of nonmetricity-mediated chiral separation effects driven by the fluid's vorticity and the Weyl magnetic field. A second nonminimal coupling of fermionic matter to metric-affine geometries proposed in the literature is also discussed.

hep-th.title: Which scale breaks quarkonium? A controlled comparison of density and momentum relaxation in holographic QCD
hep-th.author: Wenxing Cheng, Yunxianghui Wang, Zi-qiang Zhang
hep-th.abstract: In a quark-gluon plasma (QGP) that is both dense and dissipative, do static color screening and thermodynamic response follow the same medium scale? The question matters because heavy-quark observables are routinely used to infer QGP properties, yet in a background with only finite density, or only momentum relaxation, the two scales cannot be compared: one of them is absent. We use the Einstein-Maxwell-axion geometry, in which the chemical potential $\mu$ and the translational-symmetry-breaking parameter $\beta$ enter as independent controls, to carry out this comparison at fixed temperature. The static potential, the thermal free energy, and the running coupling are computed with high numerical precision, and the zero-temperature limit is used to isolate the non-thermal response. The comparison reveals a hierarchy that is invisible when either scale is studied alone: $\mu$ controls the potential and the running coupling through near-horizon color screening, while $\beta$ controls the thermal free energy through its imprint on horizon entropy. At $T=0$ the hierarchy persists in the dissociation scale, where finite density shortens the binding range far more efficiently than pure momentum relaxation. The geometric origin is that the $\mu^2 z^4$ term grows toward the horizon and deforms the region that governs string screening, whereas the constant $\beta^2$ term shifts the horizon entropy without a comparable localized deformation. This separation yields a criterion for identifying which medium scale is at work in any holographic construction that contains both density and dissipation.

hep-th.title: Hamiltonian formulation of Carrollian Maxwell theory in Deformed Light-cone Kaluza-Klein-like Null reduction
hep-th.author: Limin Zeng
hep-th.abstract: We construct magnetic and electric Carrollian Maxwell theories by performing Kaluza--Klein-like null reduction of a complex Maxwell field in a Bargmann deformed light-cone background with manifest gauge symmetry. The procedure preserves the original first-class U(1) Gauss constraint in the standard Carrollian Maxwell theories and deformed Carrollian Maxwell theories with a decoupled electric/magnetic scalar $A_-$. We give the scaling of the parent gauge parameter and show that the U(1) symmetry is inherited from the parent theory and not introduced after the limit. We emphasize that $A_-$ can be rendered non-dynamical by imposing additional ad hoc constraints. Since $A_-$ is invariant under the original U(1) symmetry, removing it is a constraint and not a gauge choice, but the resulting theory is the same as the one reached by imposing the light-cone gauge $A_- = 0$ prior to the KK-like null reduction. For an electric pseudo-coupled theory without gauge symmetry, after imposing the ad hoc constraints the theory becomes the standard electric Maxwell theory together with a decoupled zero-energy scalar $A_-$. Furthermore, our work provides an explicit example of the correct application of this approach, thereby broadening the scope of its applicability to gauge theories.

hep-th.title: From Fredholm Determinants to AdS/CFT Observables: A Universal Strong-Coupling Framework
hep-th.author: Bercel Boldis, Dennis le Plat
hep-th.abstract: We investigate the trans-series structure of the cusp anomalous dimension of $\mathcal{N}=4$ supersymmetric Yang-Mills theory and the dynamically generated mass gap of the $\mathrm{O}(6)$ sigma model at strong 't Hooft coupling. We consider the one-parameter deformation of the cusp anomalous dimension, known as the tilted cusp, and review its strong-coupling expansion obtained through its representation in terms of Fredholm determinants with a matrix Bessel kernel. The advantage of this deformation is that the non-perturbative scales separate naturally, revealing structures that remain hidden in the physical limit. Motivated by this observation, we introduce the tilted mass gap, which reduces to the physical $\mathrm{O}(6)$ mass gap at a special value of the deformation parameter and exhibits a deep connection with the tilted cusp. This formulation allows us to determine the complete strong-coupling trans-series and resurgence structure of the $\mathrm{O}(6)$ mass gap, while extending and proving conjectured relations between successive non-perturbative corrections. Building on the underlying Fredholm determinant representation, we construct an Alien calculus that generates all non-perturbative sectors of these AdS/CFT observables directly from their perturbative expansions. Finally, we derive an exact all-orders relation between the strong-coupling trans-series of the $\mathrm{O}(6)$ mass gap and the cusp anomalous dimension of planar $\mathcal{N}=4$ supersymmetric Yang-Mills theory.

hep-th.title: Effective field equations with stochastic initial conditions
hep-th.author: Ian G. Moss
hep-th.abstract: The evolution of quantum field expectation values from an initial non-equilibrium quantum state can be followed numerically using the Truncated Wigner technique. It can track non-perturbative quantum phenomena, such as false vacuum decay, in real time with promising results. Nevertheless, it is an approximate method subject to quantum loop corrections. The extension of Truncated Wigner into a fully fledged effective field equation approach is discussed here, including corrections from higher loops and higher momenta.

hep-th.title: Decoupling saddles of the gravitational index and the Farey tail
hep-th.author: Davide Cassani, Alejandro Ruipérez, Enrico Turetta
hep-th.abstract: We first construct general saddles of the five-dimensional gravitational supersymmetric index with $S^1\times\mathbb{R}^4$ asymptotics, carrying an arbitrary number of electric charges and Gibbons-Hawking centers. We then uplift the three-charge configurations to type IIB supergravity, obtaining solutions asymptotic to $S^1\times \mathbb{R}^4\times S^1\times {\rm K}3$, carrying D1-D5-P charges. Upon taking a decoupling limit, these solutions yield asymptotically Euclidean AdS$_3\times S^3\times {\rm K}3$ candidate saddles of the dual CFT$_2$ elliptic genus. We focus on the two-center saddles, which involve three integers specifying an orbifold action. Depending on these integers, the saddles may or may not possess a Euclidean horizon, and may be smooth or exhibit orbifold singularities. We give the on-shell action of these two-center saddles in the appropriate ensemble and establish a precise match with the Farey-tail expansion of the elliptic genus at the level of saddle-point actions. The horizonless saddles are the Euclidean version of fractional spectral-flow solutions previously discussed in the literature, corresponding to $({\rm AdS}_3\times S^3)/\mathbb{Z}_k$ orbifolds. The black hole saddles are modular images of the horizonless ones. They generalize the well-known ${\rm SL}(2,\mathbb{Z})$ family of BTZ black holes by placing it in the background of the $\mathbb{Z}_k$ orbifold. We also consider the asymptotically AdS$_3\times S^3$ solutions arising as decoupling limit of five-dimensional black ring and black lens saddles, provide their on-shell action and confirm that they do not contribute to the D1-D5 elliptic genus.

hep-th.title: Covariant Phase Space and Carroll-Weyl $χ$ Symmetry of Carroll Non-BPS D$_p$-branes
hep-th.author: Limin Zeng
hep-th.abstract: We analyze the covariant phase space of Klusoň's canonical Carroll non-BPS D$_p$-brane actions. The Carroll limit is formulated as a contraction of the canonical phase space: the canonical one-form is invariant under the scaling of conjugate pairs, while the leading Hamiltonian constraint differs between the electric-like and magnetic-like sectors. This difference controls the weak closure of the electric-like constraint algebra and the stronger closure of the magnetic-like Hamiltonian brackets. We separate the generic non-BPS sector, which carries $D-1$ local phase-space degrees of freedom, from the tachyon-vacuum sector, which carries $D-2$ only after imposing second-class background conditions. We also identify the rank condition for the generic electric-like sector and its strengthening in the vacuum sector. Finally, we show that the Carroll--Weyl $\chi$ transformation, the matter-sector analogue of the null-string Carroll--Weyl symmetry, preserves the symplectic form and admits a charge, but is obstructed by the constraints and cannot be promoted to a first-class gauge generator except in highly restricted corners, a global vacuum sector or the singular potential $V\propto T^{-1}$ at $p=1$. The obstruction is algebraic in $\chi$, so no restriction of its spacetime profile can remove it. This contrasts with null string theory, where a restricted $\chi$-symmetry can be completed to an additional first-class constraint.

hep-th.title: A $dS_4$ maximum in M-theory from Casimir energies on Riemann-flat manifolds
hep-th.author: Miquel Aparici, Bruno Valeixo Bento, Miguel Montero
hep-th.abstract: We describe a fully explicit, four-dimensional, top-down de Sitter saddle, constructed via compactification of M-theory on the Riemann-flat manifold $T^7/\mathbb{Z}_8$. The solution has a vacuum energy of $5.02\cdot 10^{-10}\,M_\text{Pl}^4$, a hierarchy $m_{KK}/H\sim 10^{2}$, and is under control with respect to higher loop and higher-derivative corrections. The solution has an internal manifold with a diameter of a few Planck lengths, and it may be unstable due to loops of virtual 11d black hole microstates. While the solution is the first example of a top-down dS maximum from Riemann-flat manifolds in four dimensions and is realised explicitly enough to compute the vacuum energy precisely and the spectrum of light fields, it is far from being phenomenologically viable. The solution also suggests several promising directions in the search for higher quality dS saddles in the Riemann-flat Landscape, which we describe.

hep-th.title: Allowable complex saddles with real charges in the gravitational index
hep-th.author: Fabio Billiato, Gianmarco Esposto
hep-th.abstract: We present a new supersymmetric, non-extremal complexification of asymptotically $\mathrm{AdS}$ black holes, characterized by real charges and multiple complex horizons. We investigate whether these solutions define admissible supersymmetric saddles of the gravitational path integral by applying the Kontsevich-Segal-Witten (KSW) criterion, and compare the resulting gravitational constraints with the convergence conditions of the dual superconformal index. For most of the cases studied, the KSW criterion in the asymptotic region agrees with the index convergence, while the full bulk condition is more stringent and excludes saddles whose chemical potentials lie within the index-convergence domain.

hep-th.title: Segre determinants and MHV gravity amplitudes
hep-th.author: Joris Koefler, Emanuele Ventura, Hongmiao Yu
hep-th.abstract: We describe a Segre-Veronese construction of polynomial solutions to the interpolation conditions of the numerators of tree-level MHV gravity amplitudes given by Hodges' formula. The five- and six-point Hodges numerators arise from Segre determinants, while for every $n\geq7$ suitable Segre determinants lead to solutions linearly independent of the Hodges numerator. The existence of such independent elements for $n=7,8$ was recently established by Mai and Zhang.

hep-th.title: The Komar charges of type II supergravity and supersymmetric localization
hep-th.author: Gabriele Barbagallo, Tomás Ortín
hep-th.abstract: We compute the on-shell closed, generalized Komar charges associated to an arbitrary Killing vector of the two 10-dimensional $\mathcal{N}=2$ supergravity theories which are the low-energy effective field theories of the type~IIA and IIB superstrings. We study different rewritings of this charge in terms of Page charges and forms with special properties that are used in the derivation of thermodynamical relations in black $p$-brane spacetimes. The, we show that, when the Killing vector is the supersymmetric Killing vector built as a bilinear of a Killing spinor, the momentum maps of the different fields of the theory are

hep-th.title: Possible Microscopic source of torsion
hep-th.author: A. Capolupo, S. Monda, G. Pisacane, A. Quaranta, R. Serao
hep-th.abstract: Axial fermionic interactions connect vacuum condensation with torsionful back- grounds. We consider a quartic spin spin interaction whose mean field reduction yields a quadratic fermionic Hamiltonian. Its diagonalisation defines a particle and antiparticle condensate, while self consistency determines whether the vacuum devel- ops a non zero axial current. Cutoff, fluctuation and energy conditions delimit the validity of the approximation. When torsion couples to spin, this axial expectation value can provide a microscopic source for an axial torsion background. We then consider mixed Dirac fields on such a background. In the explicit neutrino analysis, metric curvature is neglected while torsion modifies the flavour Bogoliubov coeffi- cients, producing spin dependent oscillation frequencies, condensate densities and CP asymmetries.

hep-th.title: Random Euclidean CFT$_2$ from Triangulated dS$_3$ Gravity
hep-th.author: Ji-seong Chae
hep-th.abstract: We propose a random Euclidean CFT description of three-dimensional de Sitter gravity, with fixed central charge and primary spectrum but fluctuating operator product coefficients. Our construction starts from compact regions assembled from generalized hyperbolic tetrahedra. We analytically continue the gravitational amplitudes computed from these triangulations to de Sitter parameters and use them to infer OPE correlations. We recover matching normalized amplitudes from a complex Liouville cosmological wavefunction. For the tetrahedral $K_4$ filling, the non-Gaussian OPE cumulant carries an oscillatory hyperbolic-volume phase. We reconstruct the associated Lorentzian de Sitter spacetime and show that angle derivatives of this phase yield the rapidities of boost holonomies around its initial singularity. Its spacelike future boundary carries a positive-definite conformal metric, while the wavefunction obeys Euclidean conformal Ward identities. The physical CFT spectrum is organized by integer spin, and the scalar restriction of the two-chiral fusion coefficient yields the Virasoro $6j$ square. We construct a positive finite OPE ensemble that reproduces the theta normalization and Virasoro tetrahedral cumulant while satisfying the retained sphere-crossing equations.

hep-th.title: Vacuum Polarization, Geodesic Equation and Sachs-Wolfe Effect
hep-th.author: Ali Kaya
hep-th.abstract: We show that the null geodesic equation for photons is modified in the presence of a charged scalar field, with quantum fluctuations acting as an effective mass term that changes the null paths to timelike curves. This effect can be interpreted as a vacuum polarization phenomenon in curved spacetime. The resulting contribution to the Sachs-Wolfe effect varies with photon frequency, leading to frequency-dependent corrections to the cosmic microwave background (CMB) blackbody spectrum in the form of a $\mu$-distortion, as well as modifications to the CMB power spectrum. We estimate these within a standard inflationary scenario and find that while the correction to the CMB power spectrum is significant when the scalar field is light, the magnitude of the $\mu$-distortion depends strongly on the regularization prescription.

hep-th.title: Hall's Exact Uncertainty Relation and the Geometry of Krylov-Space Operator Dynamics
hep-th.author: Mohsen Alishahiha, Souvik Banerjee
hep-th.abstract: Krylov representations of operator dynamics encode two inequivalent motions: probability transport along the discrete Krylov chain and motion of the normalized amplitude vector on the associated sphere. We lift Hall's exact uncertainty relation to Liouville space and show that, for the fixed Krylov-basis measurement, its classical Fisher information locally attains the quantum Fisher information. The amplitude vector therefore follows an exact constant-speed spherical trajectory. We construct its moving frame, identifying the first Lanczos coefficient with the speed and the higher coefficients with successive bending. Geodesic curvature controls the leading departure from Mandelstam-Tamm saturation. Separately, we compare cumulative and pointwise bounds on Krylov-index transport, which depends on the full Lanczos sequence.

hep-th.title: A large size of the pion-like excitations in the stringy fluid above $T_{ch}$ is model independent and required by current algebra
hep-th.author: L. Ya. Glozman
hep-th.abstract: Multiple lattice evidences support the existence of a confining but chirally symmetric stringy fluid regime of QCD above the chiral symmetry restoration temperature at T_{ch} ~ 155 MeV. This regime is characterized by an approximate chiral spin symmetry and its extensions which means that the propagating excitations represent the chirally symmetric quarks connected into color singlets by the chromoelectric string. Clear \pi,\pi' peaks above T_{ch} were extracted on the lattice from the spatial and temporal correlators, which become broader with temperature and disappear roughly at $3T_{ch}$. The meson-like excitations above T_{ch} were studied within the manifestly confining and chirally symmetric model. It has been demonstrated that the chiral symmetry restoration in the confining regime happens because of Pauli blocking of the levels, required for the existence of the quark condensate, by the thermal quark excitation. The same Pauli blocking leads to a huge swelling of the low-spin mesons above T_{ch} which become infinitely large in the chiral limit. This property should be crucial for the explanation of the high collectivity and a very small mean-free path of the constituents above $T_{ch}$ seen experimentally. Here we demonstrate that the swelling of pions above T_{ch} is a model-independent effect required by current algebra.

hep-th.title: Integral representations of quantum Rényi divergences on von Neumann algebras
hep-th.author: Tanay Kibe, Pratik Roy
hep-th.abstract: We prove an integral representation of the $\alpha$-$z$ Rényi divergences for normal states on arbitrary von Neumann algebras. Along each ray $z=c\alpha$, the divergence is a positive average of relative entropies evaluated in a canonical family of escort states. For orders $\alpha$ above one, we require the divergence to be finite, whereas for orders below one support inclusion suffices. An explicit boundary correction removes the lower-order support assumption. The proof uses a compatible weighted Haagerup $L^p$ scale and applies outside the data-processing region. For faithful density matrices, we express the derivative of the escort relative entropy with respect to the Rényi order in terms of a nonnegative fluctuation quantity. Differences of order-one derivatives of the divergence give quantum Fisher information and Wigner-Yanase skew information. For faithful bipartite density matrices, we also express optimized conditional $\alpha$-$z$ entropies at orders above one as averages of ordinary conditional entropies. Further applications concern coherent-state divergences in quantum field theory and the optimizing order for the strong converse exponent in hypothesis-testing.

hep-th.title: Radial Stability of Charged Interacting Quark Stars Revisited
hep-th.author: Yann Bissessur, Michael Gammon, Robert B. Mann
hep-th.abstract: An error in the charged quark star literature \cite{Goncalves:2020joq} has resulted in erroneous solutions to the radial stability equations for charged interacting quark stars in \cite{zhang:2021}. In this article we recalculate the fundamental radial eigenfrequencies for charged, interacting quark stars in general relativity and discuss any departure from previous results \cite{zhang:2021}. Most of the qualitative trends persist, but the magnitudes of the separation between the maximum mass and stability points on a given branch can change significantly. We also note that all branches in \cite{zhang:2021} that contained no stable solutions now have stable solutions in their corrected counterparts. The net effect is that in all of the studied cases charged quark stars have a greater range of stability than originally predicted. We also compare four recent observational constraints not included in previous studies, and find that these constraints are satisfied by a subset of the mass-radius relations we obtain.

hep-th.title: Lipshitz-Sarkar refines mirrors more than Khovanov
hep-th.author: Yang-Hui He
hep-th.abstract: Lipshitz and Sarkar asked in an ICM 2018 question whether their homotopy-theoretic refinement of Khovanov homology can detect mirror reflection when ordinary integral Khovanov homology cannot. We give an affirmative answer by presenting a prime knot whose integral Khovanov homology agrees with that of its mirror in every bidegree, including torsion, and yet over $\mathbb{F}_2$, the second Steenrod square has rank one for the knot and rank zero for its mirror in a specified bidegree. We also give a composite example. The construction, search and computations are done with the help of {\it chat-GTP 5.6 sol Pro} combing over the {\it Regina Census} of knots.

hep-th.title: Grey-body factor from correspondence with quasinormal mode for gravitational perturbation of higher-dimensional Reissner-Nordström black hole
hep-th.author: Hyewon Han, Bogeun Gwak
hep-th.abstract: We study the correspondence between quasinormal modes (QNMs) and grey-body factors (GBFs) of higher-dimensional Reissner--Nordström black holes. Considering scalar, vector, and tensor gravitational perturbations, we systematically compute the QNMs and GBFs for each spacetime dimension and set of black-hole parameters to evaluate the analytical formula connecting them. QNMs are obtained by the continued fraction and the integration-through-midpoints methods depending on the singularity structure in the Frobenius series. We compare the GBFs determined by the correspondence using QNMs with those computed numerically. The correspondence performs well for scalar($+$), vector($+$), vector($-$), and tensor perturbations. For the scalar($-$) perturbation, the GBFs obtained by the correspondence deviate noticeably from the accurate GBFs for black holes with low to intermediate values of the charge in $D>6$. The correspondence recovers reasonable accuracy at higher charges, although the effective potential exhibits double peaks, contrary to the assumption underlying the Wentzel--Kramers--Brillouin (WKB)-based derivation of the correspondence. Whereas the accuracy decreases with increasing $D$ for other perturbation types, the correspondence for the scalar($-$) perturbation yields more accurate GBFs in $D=8$ than those in $D=7$. For near-extreme black holes, the correspondence offers a reliable approximation of GBFs for the vector($-$) perturbation, even though a double-peak potential occurs in $D>6$. These results suggest that the correspondence has a wider range of applicability than might be expected from the assumption of the WKB approach.

hep-th.title: Gravitational Memory: an approximate description
hep-th.author: Q.-L. Zhao, P.-M. Zhang, M. Elbistan, J. Balog, P. A. Horvathy
hep-th.abstract: Plane gravitational waves play a role both in relativistic and in non-relativisitic physics, highlighted by two different mass parameters. The large-distance behaviour of a sandwich gravitational wave can be approximated by a continuous but not necessarily smooth profile, providing us with a simplified description of particle motion. Our model is consistent with the Carroll symmetry. Our strategy is illustrated by the Pöschl-Teller profile. The limitations of the sandwich approximation are discussed.

hep-th.title: Analytical Time-Domain Waveforms for Black-Hole Scattering in the Self-Force Expansion
hep-th.author: Chris Kavanagh, Julio Parra-Martinez, Davide Usseglio
hep-th.abstract: We obtain a systematic understanding of the time-domain gravitational waveform of hyperbolic black-hole scattering at first order in the self-force expansion and all orders in the post-Newtonian/post-Minkowskian (PN/PM) expansion. The continuous frequency spectrum of unbound orbits makes the inverse Fourier transform to the time domain diverge order by order; we introduce a dimensional-regularization-inspired prescription that cures this uniformly. We show that the full waveform then follows, at any PM and PN order, from a single family of integrals, generated by the Lauricella function $F_D^{(3)}$, which we calculate using strategies familiar from the study of Feynman integrals. As a proof of principle, we use this understanding to compute the quadrupolar 1SF waveform through relative 10PM-20PN, that is to order ${\cal O}(G^{10} v^{42})$, the full 1SF waveform to 10PM-10PN, as well as the asymptotic fluxes and the dissipative scattering angle at the corresponding accuracy.

hep-th.title: A Casimir turning point as the beginning of a small flat universe
hep-th.author: Alan Zhang
hep-th.abstract: We study a flat three-torus universe whose contraction is turned around by the negative Casimir energy of Standard Model fields. The trace anomaly forbids conformal matter alone to turn an anisotropic universe around, so matter with $w<1/3$, most cheaply a positive potential, must supply the negative trace; with antiperiodic fermions the Standard Model supplies the negative energy, and the universe turns at an edge of 722 reduced Planck lengths. The turning point can hold only about five quanta of the lowest modes, whereas a reheating coupling in a time-symmetric past would produce radiation exceeding the Casimir energy by at least $10^{94}$, so we read the turn as a beginning rather than a bounce. Negative Casimir energy cannot hold the shape of the torus: its shape state can be real at most once, and for a real Gaussian state survival of the shape on both branches with $90\%$ probability requires that moment to lie within $0.35$ Hubble times of the turn. The natural state, real at the turn, freezes the torus into a nearly rectangular box whose sides typically differ by $16$--$18\%$. The microwave background can read this fossil only if the shortest cycle lies between $0.985$ and about $1.04$ last-scattering diameters. At the turn the Higgs quartic coupling is negative, yet zero-point fluctuations of the gauge zero modes keep the Higgs zero mode near the origin with probability above one half for a top-quark pole mass below $172.96$ GeV, given a curvature coupling $\xi_H\gtrsim0.08$; a pole mass above $173.7$ GeV, within reach of FCC-ee, would exclude this beginning.
